data.title: Micron expects even tighter supply in 2027-28 than 2026; continues to work with Nvidia
data.description:
Micron Technology (MU) said it expects a tighter memory supply for calendar years 2027 and 2028 than in 2026 during the TomorrowX Summit in Austin on Wednesday.

"We have said before that calendar years 2027 and 2028 will be even tighter than 2026," said Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra. "Seventy-five percent of our 2027 is sold out. We are in discussions with customers now moving to 2028. Look, I mean, AI as it scales, the frontier models get larger, agentic AI usage, larger context windows, all of this just needs more memory and storage. So, our business fundamentals continue to be very, very strong. We delivered a record 2026; 2027 is going to be even stronger."

He also noted that the memory market has changed dramatically regarding long-term agreements. Historically, a memory maker would consider a one-year agreement as long-term. However, the company is now inking five-year deals through Strategic Customer Agreements, or SCAs. 

"Many of these SCAs are five-year agreements with the customers, and that is really important because five-year agreements give you that visibility into the demand," Mehrotra said. 

"This is very different compared to anything in the past," he added. "Memory is absolutely a key enabler for the customers in terms of driving best token economics, highest efficiency for their compute platforms, getting the highest ROI on their investments. In a given compute platform, you put more memory, you put faster memory, and you are able to get a higher ROI from that."

The Micron CEO also provided remarks regarding former Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang.

"I mean, Jensen, I am a huge admirer of Jensen for all his pioneering work with modern AI as well as the GPU revolution," Mehrotra said. "We worked closely with Jensen and his team, and some of the examples of HBM and pushing the envelope with respect to performance on HBM, HBM4 being an example, HBM3E, pushing it toward higher die stack and lower power. Our two companies co-innovated very many products. Of course, our relationship with NVIDIA is across all levels, multiple levels of engineering. These relationships have been built over time, and we look forward to continuing to work with the NVIDIA team as they navigate through their leadership transition."

data.title: GTA 6 launch crash? Oddsmakers call it a toss-up
data.description:
Oddsmakers are calling a Grand Theft Auto 6 server outage a coin flip ahead of its Thursday launch.

Betting marketplace BetOline is asking whether PlayStation, Xbox, or Rockstar will go down on Thursday, listing both "yes" and "no" at dead-even -120 odds.

The toss-up pricing comes as PlayStation Network is already faltering hours before the game unlocks at midnight in the U.S. Outage tracker Downdetector has logged thousands of complaints—mostly login failures and connection errors—with reports climbing sharply Wednesday after noon to nearly 1,800 at the time of writing.

While U.S. gamers are still waiting, rolling midnight releases have already brought players online in countries such as Australia and New Zealand.

To ease the strain on their networks, Sony (SONY) and Microsoft (MSFT) have both urged players to pre-download the roughly 212-gigbyte file ahead of time.

Early reviews of Grand Theft Auto 6 are strong, with IGN calling it "unprecedented, unbelievable, and unmissable," while Vice said it is Rockstar Games' "Magnus Opus," sending Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO) stock surging roughly 7%.

The Metacritic score for the game is currently at 99 out of 100, which matches the highest score of all time. A recent estimate puts Grand Theft Auto 6 close to 15M digital preorders ahead of launch.

data.title: MP Materials moves higher as Needham resumes coverage with Buy rating
data.description:
MP Materials (MP) jumped 3.8% in Wednesday's trading as Needham resumed coverage with a Buy rating and $48 price target, believing it is in the early innings of a multi-year transformation from a legacy mining company into a vertically integrated rare earth materials and permanent magnet manufacturer capable of supporting key domestic customers.

The company has made steady progress over the past year building out its integrated platform and is expected to meet key milestones in materials and magnet production in H2 2026 and 2027, Needham analyst James Ricchiuti wrote, and with long-term support from the U.S. government as a 15% stakeholder and supply agreements with anchor customers GM and Apple, MP (MP) looks poised to become a major domestic permanent magnet supplier over the next three years.

MP (MP) is extending its heavy rare earth elements refining capability at the flagship Mountain Pass, California, integrated mining and refining facility—by far the biggest operation of its kind in North America—expanding processing output and magnet manufacturing at its Independence, Texas, facility supporting its GM supply deal, and has started construction on the new $1.25B 10X permanent magnet manufacturing plant in Northland, Texas, with commissioning planned for late 2028, Ricchiuti noted.

data.title: Global-e outlines 2026 revenue $1.329B-$1.353B and adjusted EBITDA $290M-$300M, driven by Managed Markets V2 and Passport integration
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Global-E Online Ltd. (GLBE) Q3 2026

Management View

  • Amir Schlachet (Co-Founder, CEO & Chairman of the Board) said “Q3 was another strong quarter of top line growth and margin expansion” and added the company is “once again raising our outlook for GMV, revenue and adjusted EBITDA for the remainder of the year,” with 2026 expected growth of “37.6%, 39.4% and 48.6%, respectively,” and “more than $1.3 billion expected in revenues for the year, generating close to $300 million in adjusted EBITDA.”
  • Schlachet highlighted operational focus areas including Passport integration (“Passport is now our default standard shipping solution being offered to any new U.S.-based merchant”), Managed Markets V2 adoption (“managed markets starting to surpass those of our enterprise business”), duty drawback progress (“receiving approval from the CBP to be able to reclaim duties on returned goods from the U.S.”), and AI-related commerce trends (“Quarterly AI sourced browsing and checkout volumes approximately doubled in Q3 compared with the prior quarter”).
  • Ofer Koren (Chief Financial Officer) said “Q3 was another very strong quarter” and noted results “include for the first time, the contribution of Passport,” adding “Passport service fee share was lower than we expected, while fulfillment, which represents the majority of revenue was higher.”
  • Nir Debbi (Co-Founder, President & Director) attributed mix effects to larger merchants, saying “The share of merchants that are over $20 million in goods sold through our platform since Q1 '25 grew more than 50% on the platform.”

Outlook

  • Ofer Koren (Chief Financial Officer) guided Q4 2026 GMV to $3.085 billion to $3.245 billion, revenue to $464 million to $488 million, and adjusted EBITDA to $113.5 million to $123.5 million (24.9% margin at the midpoint).
  • Koren raised full-year 2026 guidance to GMV of $8.95 billion to $9.117 billion, revenue of $1.329 billion to $1.353 billion, and adjusted EBITDA of $290 million to $300 million (22% margin at the midpoint), stating the uplift is “supported by operating leverage and utilization of AI.”
  • Management emphasized Passport is incorporated in guidance and “performing in line with expectations,” with Koren saying the company “remained with our previous forecast for Passport for the remaining of the year.”

Financial Results

  • Ofer Koren (Chief Financial Officer) reported Q3 GMV of $2.042 billion and total revenue of $314 million, including services revenue of $134 million and fulfillment services revenue of $180.1 million “including the contribution of Passport.”
  • Koren reported non-GAAP gross profit of $140.6 million (44.8% non-GAAP gross margin) and GAAP gross profit of $133.9 million (42.6% margin), adding that “Excluding Passport, our non-GAAP gross margin in Q3 was slightly higher compared to our Q2 margin.”
  • Koren reported adjusted EBITDA of $63.7 million (20.3% margin), non-GAAP net profit of $63 million and non-GAAP net profit per share of $0.37; GAAP net profit was $81.1 million and GAAP EPS was $0.47, with GAAP net profit “positively impacted” by “a release of the valuation allowance on our deferred tax assets.”
  • Koren said Q3 ended with $347 million in cash and cash equivalents (including short-term deposits and marketable securities) and free cash flow of $66.4 million.
  • Amir Schlachet (Co-Founder, CEO & Chairman of the Board) said the company repurchased “approximately $53 million worth of shares” in Q3; Koren added there was “approximately $446 million of remaining capacity under the $500 million plan as of the end of the quarter.”

Q&A

  • Andrew Bauch, BMO Capital Markets: asked about Managed Markets acceleration and durability; Amir Schlachet (Co-Founder, CEO & Chairman of the Board) said drivers included “managed pricing on shipping,” “opening of the new markets,” and Shopify featuring it, and added “we expect that to continue into 2027.” Bauch also asked about Passport mix; Ofer Koren (Chief Financial Officer) said Passport revenue was in line but “the mix was a bit different,” with “service revenue… quite low” and “the majority was fulfillment revenue.”
  • William Nance, Goldman Sachs: asked about the 50% conversion uplift and merchant mix plus take-rate trajectory; Schlachet said “the 50% rise in conversion is very encouraging,” citing both existing and new merchants and Shopify’s “Global by Default initiative”; Koren said the business is seeing “quite stable service fee take rates in the coming quarters” after the Managed Markets V2 “step change,” and pointed to volume-tiered pricing and “value-added services” as drivers.
  • Craig Maurer, FT Partners: asked about 2027 contribution from 2026 logo wins; Schlachet said “we expect these new launches to continue and be a strong driver also into 2027,” noting some launches shift past peak to “the beginning of the following year.”
  • Chao Zhang, UBS: asked about same-store sales vs. new merchant contribution and fuel surcharge impacts; Koren said same-store sales remained “strong… but not at the level that we saw in the first half,” partly due to FX, and said fuel surcharge decisions reduced gross margin in Q2 and Q3, but “Towards Q4, we did update the fuel surcharges.”
  • William Fitzsimmons, Piper Sandler: pressed on Q3 same-store sales deceleration and Global by Default timing; Koren cited weaker FX, fewer Q3 promotions, and “slightly slower” demand vs. H1; Schlachet said Global by Default applies to new Shopify merchants “using Shopify Payments” and was “turned on quite recently.”
  • Scott Berg, Needham: asked why GMV was down quarter-over-quarter; Nir Debbi (Co-Founder, President & Director) said Q2 was “indexed way above” due to promotions, and Q3 being lower “materialized as we expected.” Berg also asked about value-added services adoption; Debbi said CBP approval for “1313” duty drawback should allow first filings “by the end of the year,” while U.S. J1 duty drawback adoption is “going slower than expected” and is expected to “pick up early '27.”
  • Samad Samana, Jefferies: asked whether Shopify’s marketing changed Managed Markets merchant composition and asked about BFCM promo timing; Schlachet said “we don't see any major shifts,” with the base still “skewed towards… SMBs,” and Koren said activity starts earlier in November but “The peak is still in front of us,” with guidance based on merchant discussions and recent trading.
  • Matthew Bullock, BofA Securities: asked when agentic commerce could be meaningful; Schlachet said fully agentic transactions are “very, very early days” and “it's hard to tell when… will… be meaningful,” while Debbi cited OpenAI’s wallet announcement and said global buying may require solutions where “Global-e is based.”
  • Patrick Walravens, Citizens JMP: asked about cyber threats and 2027 growth framing; Schlachet said Global-e has “seen an increase in activity” and implemented “many more processes… also AI and agentic driven”; Koren said the company “believe[s] that 2027 will be another strong year of growth and profitability” and “in line with our multiyear framework.”
  • James Faucette, Morgan Stanley: asked about retention/pricing and build vs. buy; Debbi said attrition is “below the 4% mark” and NDR is “over the 120%,” and added the company is not focused on raising prices but on “increase our share” via logistics and “duty drawback,” while on capability expansion he said the approach is “a combination of both” acquisitions and internal builds.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were largely slightly positive and growth-focused, repeatedly pressing on Managed Markets durability, take rates, same-store sales deceleration, and seasonality; questions like “how durable that acceleration… can be?” (Andrew Bauch, BMO Capital Markets) and “why GMV would actually be down quarter-over-quarter?” (Scott Berg, Needham) reflected scrutiny on growth drivers.
  • Management tone was positive in prepared remarks and largely confident in Q&A, using phrases like “we expect that to continue into 2027” (Amir Schlachet, Co-Founder, CEO & Chairman of the Board) and “we expect… quite stable service fee take rates” (Ofer Koren, Chief Financial Officer), while acknowledging pockets of moderation (“not as positive as it was in the first half,” Koren) and slower adoption areas (“going slower than expected,” Debbi).
  • Versus the prior quarter, the discussion shifted from introducing Passport and completing Managed Markets V1-to-V2 migration to detailing Passport revenue mix, Managed Markets acceleration, and a more explicit acknowledgement of H1-to-H2 same-store sales normalization.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance language remained upwardly revised in both quarters; in Q3, management emphasized raising GMV, revenue, and adjusted EBITDA again and highlighted “meaningful acceleration across all parameters compared to 2025,” while Q2 emphasized results “beat the high end of the range across all of our guidance metrics” and adding Passport into guidance.
  • Passport moved from acquisition announcement and early integration in Q2 to operational deployment in Q3, including “completed Phase 1” integration and becoming the “default standard shipping solution” for new U.S.-based merchants, alongside CFO commentary that Passport’s revenue mix skewed more to fulfillment than expected.
  • Managed Markets V2 shifted from migration completion and early adoption commentary in Q2 to Q3 comments that “GMV growth outpaced the core business in the back half of the quarter,” with management citing managed pricing and new geographies (Canada and the U.K.).
  • Analysts’ focus evolved from V2 migration milestones and baseline impacts (Q2) to durability of V2 acceleration, take-rate implications, and intra-year GMV seasonality (Q3), with management more directly discussing H1 promotional intensity and FX effects as Q3 headwinds.

Risks and Concerns

  • Ofer Koren (Chief Financial Officer) flagged FX and moderation in same-store sales momentum, saying demand is “still strong… but not at the level that we saw in the first half,” and noted fuel surcharge timing can pressure gross margin when Global-e delays passing through carrier updates.
  • Nir Debbi (Co-Founder, President & Director) said U.S. J1 duty drawback onboarding is “going slower than expected,” attributing merchant focus to “managing their IEEPA claims,” with mitigation framed as expectations it “pick up early '27.”
  • Amir Schlachet (Co-Founder, CEO & Chairman of the Board) acknowledged higher cyber threat activity, saying Global-e has “seen an increase in activity” and is responding with “AI and agentic driven” security processes.

Final Takeaway

Management presented Q3 as continued high growth with profitability expansion, paired with higher full-year 2026 guidance and an outlook for a strong Q4. Executives emphasized Passport’s progressing integration (now default U.S. standard shipping for new merchants), accelerating Shopify Managed Markets V2 activity supported by feature launches like managed pricing, and expanding value-added services such as duty drawback following CBP approval for returned-goods reclaims. In Q&A, management acknowledged H1-to-H2 normalization in same-store sales and fuel-surcharge timing impacts, while reiterating expectations for continued Managed Markets momentum and improved Passport margin profile in 2027.

data.title: Nvidia slides as interim CEO Kress speaks to employees, says, 'Let's move forward'
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) shares slid more than 3% on Wednesday, one day after the tech giant reported better-than-expected results and raised its guidance for fiscal 2028.

Interim CEO Collette Kress addressed employees after co-founder Jensen Huang stunningly resigned this month and said, “Let's move forward,” according to CNBC, citing a person in the room who spoke on condition of anonymity.

Kress also spoke of pay raises for employees and the need for the company to move forward following Huang's resignation, which occurred after the longtime CEO admitted to infidelity and may have been the subject of a foreign intelligence operation. Nvidia's newly appointed Chairman Harvey Jones, who joined Kress on Wednesday, reaffirmed this week the company will not look to rehire Huang as CEO. (On Tuesday, Huang made his first public comments after his resignation and intimated he would be honored to return as CEO if the board of directors asked him to do so.)

Other topics that were brought up at the meeting included the search for Nvidia's next CEO, the news outlet added, citing the attendee. Kress and Jones were joined by other members of Nvidia's executive team, including Ian Buck, Jeff Fisher, Jonah Allen, Debora Shoquist, and co-founder Chris Malachowsky, the news outlet added.

Buck made his first appearance on Nvidia's conference call with Wall Street analysts on Tuesday.

The attendee added that the sentiment in the room was that some employees want Huang to return as CEO, echoing some statements from investors. On Wednesday, hedge fund manager Bill Ackman said the company's board “is not acting in the best interest of shareholders nor in a manner consistent with their fiduciary duties.”

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Seeking Alpha.

data.title: Riot Platforms, Flowserve gain after Starboard pitches at C4K Investors Conference
data.description:
Riot Platforms (RIOT) climbed 9.4%, and Flowserve (FLS) advanced 1.8% after Starboard Value pitched the ideas at the C4K Investors Conference. 

Starboard's Jeff Smith pitched the long ideas at the C4K Investors Conference in Toronto on Wednesday, according to a copy of the presentations given at the charity conference in Toronto.

Bloomberg reported in April that Starboard had built a significant stake in Flowserve (FLS) and was seeking potential changes. Starboard, in a May letter to the board, said Flowserve (FLS) must improve its margins or risk falling behind competitors.

Flowserve (FLS) can achieve high-single-digit or better revenue growth, especially with a record backlog entering its next fiscal year, Starboard said in its presentation on Wednesday. Flowserve could also achieve operating margins above 22% by 2030. 

The activist also believes disruptions in the Middle East that have delayed equipment deliveries can turn into tailwinds, the activist said at the conference. 

Starboard owned 3.4 million shares of Flowserve (FLS) as of Sept. 30, making it one of the top 10 largest holders. 

The activist argues that Riot Platforms (RIOT) can unlock more value by converting to a real estate investment trust or selling itself to an established data center REIT or infrastructure investor, according to the presentation on Wednesday.

Starboard owned 10.5 million shares of RIOT as of Sept. 30, making the firm the 5th biggest holder with a 2.8% stake. News of the Starboard pitches was earlier reported by Bloomberg.

data.title: Nissan focuses on lower costs as Chinese automakers gain ground in Mexico
data.description:
Nissan Motor (NSANY) is using its experience in Mexico to prepare for a potential challenge from Chinese automakers in the US, as the Japanese manufacturer seeks to lower production costs and rebuild its market position.

Christian Meunier, chairman of Nissan Americas, said the company is facing growing competition from Chinese brands in Mexico, where they have rapidly secured about 10% of the market. The country is serving as a testing ground for strategies that could help Nissan (NSANY) compete with lower-cost rivals if they eventually enter the US.

Meunier said Nissan (NSANY) has roughly two years to improve its cost structure before Chinese manufacturers begin producing vehicles in Mexico to avoid import tariffs. The company is pursuing shorter development cycles, simpler engineering, greater automation, and supply chain savings.

Nissan's (NSANY) immediate priority remains reviving its US business, where its market share has recovered to around 6% after declining significantly over the past decade.

The automaker is preparing a series of new models, beginning with a hybrid version of its Rogue SUV. It also plans to bring back the Xterra later in the decade as part of a broader expansion of rugged sport utility vehicles.

Although tariffs and restrictions on Chinese automotive software currently limit their US entry, Meunier believes Nissan (NSANY) must prepare for their possible arrival within five to 10 years.

data.title: U.S. aircraft carrier leaves Middle East after reinforcements arrive
data.description:
The USS George Washington carrier strike group departed the Persian Gulf region and may be returning to Yokosuka, Japan, Bloomberg News reported Wednesday, citing two U.S. officials who requested anonymity. It was one of three American carrier groups deployed to support the naval blockade against Iran.

For investors, the departure changes the military posture around a region critical to global energy supplies. It does not by itself establish that tensions are easing: the arrival of another carrier preserves US military options, leaving uncertainty over renewed fighting and potential disruption to shipping.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt strike group arrived Monday, expanding President Donald Trump’s options should he resume active hostilities against Iran. U.S. Central Command published an image Wednesday showing the Roosevelt and George Washington sailing together.

The George Washington reached the region in August, leaving the western Pacific without a U.S. aircraft carrier. Analysts had warned that China might seek to exploit that absence.

Before this year’s Iran operations, the United States last deployed three carrier strike groups to the Middle East during the opening phase of the Iraq invasion in 2003.
